title: Near 1981, sunspot counts fall relative to area at matched emission in flat-level models
abstract: We test the sunspot-count fall near 1981 with independent area and group records. At matched F10.7 in November 1978 to June 1983, sunspot number falls by 13.15%, while corrected area changes by -0.29%. Count per area falls by 12.90% (conditional 95% limits -20.21% to -4.52%). Kislovodsk-only dates, projected area, activity overlap and independent radio conditioning retain the flat-model contrast. Group counts above 100 area units also fall. But local time slopes weaken the count-per-area result and change the group response. An earlier phase control gives a larger count-per-area fall. The two area products show relative drift. These tests constrain an equal decline of counts and total area under the main model. They do not identify a counting error, smaller individual spots, or an abrupt solar transition. We provide code, model estimates, figures, source hashes and retrieval instructions. External observations stay outside the publication.
